      "file_text": "# Sidebar Extension API\n\n## Overview\n\nThe Sidebar app supports user-created extensions that add new floating components to the sidebar. Extensions are self-contained modules that can display information, accept interactions, and integrate with system APIs.\n\n## Extension Interface\n\n```swift\nprotocol SidebarExtension {\n    /// Unique identifier for the extension\n    var id: String { get }\n    \n    /// Display name shown in extension manager\n    var name: String { get }\n    \n    /// SF Symbol or emoji for the icon\n    var icon: String { get }\n    \n    /// Render the extension's UI\n    func render(context: ExtensionContext) -> some View\n    \n    /// Called when user hovers over the extension (optional)\n    func onHover() -> Void\n    \n    /// Called when user stops hovering (optional)\n    func onHoverEnd() -> Void\n    \n    /// Handle files dropped onto this extension (optional)\n    func onFileDrop(files: [URL]) -> Void\n    \n    /// Handle items dragged out of this extension (optional)\n    func onDragOut() -> [NSItemProvider]?\n    \n    /// Settings/preferences view (optional)\n    func settingsView() -> some View\n}\n```\n\n## Extension Context\n\nExtensions receive a context object that provides access to system capabilities:\n\n```swift\nstruct ExtensionContext {\n    /// Current hover state (contracted, normal, expanded)\n    let displayState: DisplayState\n    \n    /// Available height for the extension\n    let availableHeight: CGFloat\n    \n    /// Access to the clipboard\n    let clipboard: ClipboardService\n    \n    /// Access to staged files in the drop zone\n    let dropZone: DropZoneService\n    \n    /// Access to window information\n    let windowManager: WindowManagerService\n    \n    /// Persistent storage for this extension\n    let storage: ExtensionStorage\n    \n    /// Network requests (sandboxed)\n    let network: NetworkService\n    \n    /// System notifications\n    let notifications: NotificationService\n}\n\nenum DisplayState {\n    case contracted  // Other extension is hovered\n    case normal      // Status Bar (Menu Bar Replacement)\n\n**What it replaces:** macOS Menu Bar\n\n**Features:**\n- Live clock with date on hover\n- System status: WiFi, Bluetooth, battery, volume\n- Quick actions: Lock, Sleep, Settings\n- Menu bar app tray (shows background apps like 1Password, Bartender, etc.)\n- Notification indicator with badge count\n- Mini calendar popover\n\n**Behavior:**\n- Always visible at top of sidebar\n- Expands on hover to show more controls\n- Click clock for calendar view\n\n---\n\n### 2.       "code": "# Sidebar \u2014 macOS Shell Replacement\n\n## Product Vision\n\nSidebar replaces the Dock, Menu Bar, Spotlight, and Stage Manager with a unified, extensible interface on the edge of your screen. One surface for everything: launching apps, managing windows, staging files, and accessing system controls.\n\n---\n\n## Core Components\n\n### 1. Status Bar (Menu Bar Replacement)\n\n**What it replaces:** macOS Menu Bar\n\n**Features:**\n- Live clock with date on hover\n- System status: WiFi, Bluetooth, battery, volume\n- Quick actions: Lock, Sleep, Settings\n- Menu bar app tray (shows background apps like 1Password, Bartender, etc.)\n- Notification indicator with badge count\n- Mini calendar popover\n\n**Behavior:**\n- Always visible at top of sidebar\n- Expands on hover to show more controls\n- Click clock for calendar view\n\n---\n\n### 2. App Launcher (Spotlight Replacement)\n\n**What it replaces:** Spotlight, Launchpad, Raycast (partially)\n\n**Trigger:**\n- \u2318K (configurable)\n- Click search bar in sidebar\n- Configurable hot corner\n\n**Features:**\n- Full-text search across apps, files, settings, recent documents\n- Category browsing when no query\n- Pin apps directly to sidebar from results\n- Create folders to organize pinned apps\n- Quick actions: \"Open with...\", \"Show in Finder\", \"Pin to Sidebar\"\n- Recently used apps section\n- Calculator/unit conversion inline\n\n**Data sources:**\n- Native: NSMetadataQuery (Spotlight index)\n- Optional: Raycast integration if installed\n- File system watchers for /Applications, ~/Applications\n\n**Keyboard navigation:**\n- \u2191\u2193 navigate results\n- \u21b5 open app\n- \u2318\u21b5 pin to sidebar\n- \u21e5 switch between categories\n- \u238b close\n\n---\n\n### 3. Pinned Apps (Dock Replacement)\n\n**What it replaces:** macOS Dock\n\n**Features:**\n- Grid of squircle app icons (default)\n- List view with names on hover/expand\n- Running indicator (dot beneath icon)\n- Drag to reorder\n- Right-click context menu:\n  - Remove from Sidebar\n  - Open at Login\n  - Show in Finder\n  - Force Quit (if running)\n- Drop files onto app icon to open with that app\n- Folder support (group apps into collapsible folders)\n\n**Behavior:**\n- Contracts to icon-only grid by default\n- Expands to show app names and status on hover\n- Badge support for notification counts\n\n---\n\n### 4. Windows (Stage Manager Replacement)\n\n**What it replaces:** Stage Manager, App Expos\u00e9, \u2318Tab\n\n**Features:**\n- Tree view: Apps \u2192 Windows\n- Collapse/expand individual apps\n- Click window to focus\n- Hover to show preview thumbnail (optional)\n- Window controls on hover: minimize, close\n- Drag windows onto each other to create groups\n- Window groups show as nested items\n- Tiling options: left half, right half, quadrants, custom grid\n- \"Minimize All\", \"Tile All\" bulk actions\n\n**Window Grouping:**\n- Drag window A onto window B to group\n- Groups can be named\n- Click group header to focus all windows\n- Drag group to tile all grouped windows\n- Ungroup via context menu\n\n**Data source:**\n- Accessibility API (AXUIElement)\n- CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo for window metadata\n\n---\n\n### 5. Clipboard\n\n**Features:**\n- Current clipboard preview\n- History (last 20-50 items, configurable)\n- Click item to copy back to clipboard\n- Filter by type: text, images, files\n- Pin important items\n- Clear history\n- Sensitive content detection (optional: don't store passwords)\n\n**Data source:**\n- NSPasteboard polling or observer\n\n---\n\n### 6. Drop Zone\n\n**Features:**\n- Visual drop target for files\n- Staged files persist until cleared\n- Drag files out to any app or folder\n- Multi-file support\n- Clear all button\n- Individual remove buttons\n- Shows file icon and name\n\n**Behavior:**\n- Accepts: files, folders, images, URLs\n- Drag out: provides file as draggable item\n- Spring-loaded: hover over app in Pinned Apps while dragging to open that app\n\n---\n\n### 7. Extensions\n\n**Built-in extensions:**\n- Now Playing (Music, Spotify)\n- Weather\n- System Stats (CPU, RAM, Network)\n- Quick Notes\n\n**User extensions:**\n- See Extension API documentation\n- Install from gallery or manual .sidebarext files\n- Sandboxed execution\n- Permission-based access to system features\n\n---\n\n## Global Behaviors\n\n### Hover Magnification\n\nWhen hovering any component:\n- That component expands (flex: 2.2)\n- Other components contract (flex: 0.6)\n- Smooth 300ms transition\n- All components remain visible\n\n### Screen Edge Behavior\n\n**Options:**\n1. Always visible (fixed width)\n2. Auto-hide (reveal on hover at edge)\n3. Peek (narrow strip visible, expands on hover)\n\n**Multi-monitor:**\n- Choose which monitor(s) show sidebar\n- Option for independent sidebars per monitor\n- Drag windows between sidebars to move to that monitor\n\n### Keyboard Shortcuts\n\n| Shortcut | Action |\n|----------|--------|\n| \u2318K | Open launcher |\n| \u2318\u2325D | Toggle sidebar visibility |\n| \u2318\u2325W | Focus Windows component |\n| \u2318\u2325C | Focus Clipboard component |\n| \u2318\u23251-9 | Launch pinned app by position |\n\n---\n\n## Setup Flow\n\n### First Launch\n\n1. Welcome screen explaining the concept\n2. Permission requests:\n   - Accessibility (required for window management)\n   - Automation (for app control)\n   - Screen Recording (optional, for window thumbnails)\n3. \"Replace Dock?\" prompt:\n   - Option to hide system Dock\n   - Option to hide menu bar\n4. Import pinned apps:\n   - Offer to import current Dock apps\n5. Choose sidebar position (left/right)\n6. Tutorial overlay highlighting components\n\n### Migration from Dock\n\n```swift\n// Read current Dock apps\nlet dockPlist = \"~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock.plist\"\nlet persistentApps = readPlist(dockPlist)[\"persistent-apps\"]\n\n// Offer to import\nfor app in persistentApps {\n    let path = app[\"tile-data\"][\"file-data\"][\"_CFURLString\"]\n    // Add to sidebar pinned apps\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Technical Architecture\n\n### Core Framework\n\n- **Language:** Swift\n- **UI:** SwiftUI (for components) + AppKit (for system integration)\n- **Architecture:** MVVM with Pinned Apps (Dock Replacement)\\n\\n**What it replaces:** macOS Dock\\n\\n**Features:**\\n- Grid of squircle app icons (default)\\n- List view with names on hover/expand\\n- Running indicator (dot beneath icon)\\n- Drag to reorder\\n- Right-click context menu:\\n  - Remove from Sidebar\\n  - Open at Login\\n  - Show in Finder\\n  - Force Quit (if running)\\n- Drop files onto app icon to open with that app\\n- Folder support (group apps into collapsible folders)\\n\\n**Behavior:**\\n- Contracts to icon-only grid by default\\n- Expands to show app names and status on hover\\n- Badge support for notification counts\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 4. Windows (Stage Manager Replacement)\\n\\n**What it replaces:** Stage Manager, App Expos\\u00e9, \\u2318Tab\\n\\n**Features:**\\n- Tree view: Apps \\u2192 Windows\\n- Collapse/expand individual apps\\n- Click window to focus\\n- Hover to show preview thumbnail (optional)\\n- Window controls on hover: minimize, close\\n- Drag windows onto each other to create groups\\n- Window groups show as nested items\\n- Tiling options: left half, right half, quadrants, custom grid\\n- \\\"Minimize All\\\", \\\"Tile All\\\" bulk actions\\n\\n**Window Grouping:**\\n- Drag window A onto window B to group\\n- Groups can be named\\n- Click group header to focus all windows\\n- Drag group to tile all grouped windows\\n- Ungroup via context menu\\n\\n**Data source:**\\n- Accessibility API (AXUIElement)\\n- CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo for window metadata\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 5. Clipboard\\n\\n**Features:**\\n- Current clipboard preview\\n- History (last 20-50 items, configurable)\\n- Click item to copy back to clipboard\\n- Filter by type: text, images, files\\n- Pin important items\\n- Clear history\\n- Sensitive content detection (optional: don't store passwords)\\n\\n**Data source:**\\n- NSPasteboard polling or observer\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 6. Drop Zone\\n\\n**Features:**\\n- Visual drop target for files\\n- Staged files persist until cleared\\n- Drag files out to any app or folder\\n- Multi-file support\\n- Clear all button\\n- Individual remove buttons\\n- Shows file icon and name\\n\\n**Behavior:**\\n- Accepts: files, folders, images, URLs\\n- Drag out: provides file as draggable item\\n- Spring-loaded: hover over app in Pinned Apps while dragging to open that app\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 7. Extensions\\n\\n**Built-in extensions:**\\n- Now Playing (Music, Spotify)\\n- Weather\\n- System Stats (CPU, RAM, Network)\\n- Quick Notes\\n\\n**User extensions:**\\n- See Extension API documentation\\n- Install from gallery or manual .sidebarext files\\n- Sandboxed execution\\n- Permission-based access to system features\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Global Behaviors\\n\\n### Hover Magnification\\n\\nWhen hovering any component:\\n- That component expands (flex: 2.2)\\n- Other components contract (flex: 0.6)\\n- Smooth 300ms transition\\n- All components remain visible\\n\\n### Screen Edge Behavior\\n\\n**Options:**\\n1. Always visible (fixed width)\\n2. Auto-hide (reveal on hover at edge)\\n3. Peek (narrow strip visible, expands on hover)\\n\\n**Multi-monitor:**\\n- Choose which monitor(s) show sidebar\\n- Option for independent sidebars per monitor\\n- Drag windows between sidebars to move to that monitor\\n\\n### Keyboard Shortcuts\\n\\n| Shortcut | Action |\\n|----------|--------|\\n| \\u2318K | Open launcher |\\n| \\u2318\\u2325D | Toggle sidebar visibility |\\n| \\u2318\\u2325W | Focus Windows component |\\n| \\u2318\\u2325C | Focus Clipboard component |\\n| \\u2318\\u23251-9 | Launch pinned app by position |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Setup Flow\\n\\n### First Launch\\n\\n1. Welcome screen explaining the concept\\n2. Permission requests:\\n   - Accessibility (required for window management)\\n   - Automation (for app control)\\n   - Screen Recording (optional, for window thumbnails)\\n3. \\\"Replace Dock?\\\" prompt:\\n   - Option to hide system Dock\\n   - Option to hide menu bar\\n4. Import pinned apps:\\n   - Offer to import current Dock apps\\n5. Choose sidebar position (left/right)\\n6.    // Add to sidebar pinned apps\\n}\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Technical Architecture\\n\\n### Core Framework\\n\\n- **Language:** Swift\\n- **UI:** SwiftUI (for components) + AppKit (for system The app should be a floating glass panel anchored to the left or right edge of the screen with modular, vertically stacked components.\n\n**The name \"Cider\"** \u2014 phonetically \"side-r\" (it's on the side), made from apples (macOS), refreshing/crisp connotation. The logo is an amber/gold S-shaped apple peel spiral.\n\n---\n\n## Tech Stack\n\n- **Language:** Swift\n- **UI Framework:** SwiftUI for component views, AppKit for system-level integration (window management, accessibility APIs, panel behavior)\n- **Architecture:** MVVM with Combine for reactive state\n- **Target:** macOS 14+ (Sonoma and later)\n- **Build System:** Xcode / Swift Package Manager\n\nThis must feel completely native. No Electron, no web views, no cross-platform frameworks. Use NSPanel for the sidebar window so it floats above other windows without taking focus. Use the Accessibility API (AXUIElement) for window management. Use NSPasteboard for clipboard. Use NSMetadataQuery for Spotlight search integration.\n\n---\n\n## V0.1 Scope \u2014 What to Build Now\n\nBuild a minimal but functional sidebar that proves the concept. Just these features:\n\n### 1. Floating Sidebar Shell\n- An always-on-top `NSPanel` (`.nonactivatingPanel`) that floats on the left or right screen edge\n- Full height of the screen (minus menu bar)\n- Fixed width (~72px collapsed, ~280px expanded)\n- **Glassmorphism appearance:** Use `NSVisualEffectView` with `.behindWindow` material for the native macOS frosted glass look. The sidebar should feel like a translucent glass panel, consistent with macOS Tahoe/Sonoma vibrancy\n- Rounded corners on the inner edge (the edge not touching the screen border)\n- No title bar, no standard window chrome\n- Should not appear in the Dock or Cmd+Tab switcher (set `activationPolicy` to `.accessory` or `.prohibited`)\n- Should not steal focus from the active app when clicked\n\n### 2. Pinned Apps (Dock Replacement)\n- A configurable grid of app icons displayed as squircles (rounded-rect with continuous corners, like iOS/macOS app icons)\n- Users can add/remove apps (store the list in UserDefaults or a JSON config file)\n- Click an app icon to launch it or bring it to front if already running\n- Show a small dot indicator beneath running apps\n- Right-click context menu: \"Remove from Cider\", \"Show in Finder\"\n- Drag to reorder\n- For the initial version, provide a way to import current Dock apps from `~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dock.plist`\n\n### 3. Window List (Stage Manager Replacement)\n- Display all open windows grouped by application, as a tree view: App Name \u2192 Window titles\n- Collapse/expand each app group\n- Click a window entry to focus it (bring it to front and focus the app)\n- Show basic window controls on hover: a close button (\u00d7)\n- Use `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` to enumerate windows\n- Use `AXUIElement` API to focus, minimize, and close windows\n- Refresh the list reactively when windows open/close/change\n\n### 4. Hover Expand/Contract Behavior\n- The sidebar has multiple vertically stacked component sections\n- When hovering over any component, it smoothly expands (takes more vertical space) while other components contract\n- Use SwiftUI animation with ~300ms spring/easeInOut transitions\n- All components remain visible at all times \u2014 nothing fully collapses to zero height\n- Default (no hover): all components share space roughly equally\n- On hover: hovered component gets ~2.5x flex weight, others get ~0.5\u20130.6x\n\n---\n\n## Full Feature Vision (DO NOT BUILD YET \u2014 Context Only)\n\nThese are planned features for future versions. They are listed here so you understand the architecture direction and don't paint yourself into a corner. Structure the code to accommodate these later.\n\n### Status Bar (Menu Bar Replacement) \u2014 v0.3\n- Live clock with date on hover\n- System status icons: WiFi, Bluetooth, battery, volume\n- Menu bar app tray (surface background apps like 1Password, Bartender)\n- Quick actions: Lock, Sleep, Settings\n- Mini calendar popover\n\n### App Launcher / Search (Spotlight Replacement) \u2014 v0.2\n- Triggered by \u2318K (configurable), clicking search bar, or hot corner\n- Full-text search across apps, files, settings, recent documents\n- Category browsing when no query entered\n- Pin apps to sidebar from search results\n- Keyboard navigation: \u2191\u2193 navigate, \u21b5 open, \u2318\u21b5 pin, \u21e5 categories, \u238b close\n- Data sources: NSMetadataQuery (Spotlight index), /Applications file watcher\n\n### Clipboard History \u2014 v0.2\n- Show current clipboard contents as a preview\n- Keep history of last 20\u201350 items (configurable)\n- Click any item to re-copy it to clipboard\n- Filter by type: text, images, files\n- Pin important items\n- Sensitive content detection (optionally skip passwords)\n- Data source: NSPasteboard polling\n\n### File Drop Zone \u2014 v0.3\n- A visual drop target area in the sidebar\n- Drag files from Finder/desktop into the drop zone to \"stage\" them\n- Staged files persist until manually cleared\n- Drag files back out of the drop zone into any app or folder\n- Multi-file support, individual remove buttons, clear all\n- Spring-loaded behavior: hover over a pinned app icon while dragging to open that app\n\n### Window Grouping & Tiling \u2014 v0.3\n- Drag one window entry onto another to create a group\n- Groups can be named\n- Tiling options: left half, right half, quadrants, custom grid\n- \"Minimize All\", \"Tile All\" bulk actions\n\n### Extension System \u2014 v0.4\n- Plugin architecture for user-created sidebar components\n- `CiderExtension` protocol: id, name, icon, render(), onHover(), onFileDrop(), settingsView()\n- `ExtensionContext` provides: display state, clipboard service, drop zone service, window manager service, persistent storage, sandboxed networking\n- Extensions packaged as `.ciderext` bundles with manifest.json\n- Built-in extensions: Now Playing, Weather, System Stats, Quick Notes\n- Security: sandboxed execution, permission-based access\n\n### Pawkit Integration \u2014 v1.0\n- Cider is the capture/interaction layer; Pawkit (a separate app) is the organization/storage brain\n- Clipboard \u2192 \ud83d\udc3e button to save URLs/text to Pawkit\n- Drop Zone \u2192 save staged files to Pawkit library\n- Pawkit extension panel: recent items, tag buttons, search, quick actions\n- Communication via local API, REST API, or shared SQLite database\n\n### Multi-Monitor Support \u2014 v0.3\n- Choose which monitors show the sidebar\n- Option for independent sidebar per monitor\n- Drag windows between sidebars to move between monitors\n\n### Setup Flow \u2014 v1.0\n- Welcome screen explaining the concept\n- Permission requests: Accessibility (required), Automation, Screen Recording (optional)\n- \"Replace Dock?\" prompt that hides the system Dock\n- Import current Dock apps into Cider pinned apps\n- Choose sidebar position (left/right)\n- Tutorial overlay\n\n### Dock Hiding\n```swift\n// Hide the Dock when Cider replaces it\nfunc hideDock() {\n autohide-time-modifier\")\n    shell(\"killall Dock\")\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Guidelines\n\n### Project Structure\n```\nCider/\n\u251c\u2500\u2500 App/\n\u2502   \u251c\u2500\u2500 Decisions\n\n1. **NSPanel, not NSWindow** \u2014 The sidebar must float above other windows without taking focus. Use `NSPanel` with `.nonactivatingPanel` style mask and set `hidesOnDeactivate = false`, `canBecomeKey = false`, `level = .floating`.\n\n2. **NSHostingView for SwiftUI** \u2014 Host SwiftUI views inside the NSPanel via `NSHostingView`. This gives you the best of both worlds: AppKit for system integration, SwiftUI for UI components.\n\n3. **Accessibility API permission** \u2014 The app MUST request and check Accessibility permissions on first launch. Without this, window management cannot work. Use `AXIsProcessTrusted()` to check, and guide the user to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility if needed.\n\n4. **Combine for reactive updates** \u2014 Use `@Published` properties in ViewModels and Combine publishers for window list changes, clipboard updates, etc.\n\n5. **NSVisualEffectView for glassmorphism** \u2014 Wrap the sidebar content in `NSVisualEffectView` with material `.hudWindow` or `.popover` and blending mode `.behindWindow` for the native frosted glass effect.\n\n6. **App icon rendering** \u2014 Use `NSWorkspace.shared.icon(forFile:)` to get app icons. For squircle shape, use `.clipShape(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous))`.\n\n7. **Window enumeration** \u2014 Use `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo([.optionOnScreenOnly, .excludeDesktopElements], kCGNullWindowID)` to get the window list. Filter out Cider's own windows. Map to `WindowInfo` model structs.\n\n8. **Window focusing** \u2014 To focus a window: get the owning app's PID, create an `AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)`, get the windows array, find the matching window, call `AXUIElementPerformAction(window, kAXRaiseAction)` and activate the app via `NSRunningApplication.activate()`.\n\n9. **Persisting pinned apps** \u2014 Store as an array of bundle identifiers in UserDefaults or a JSON file at `~/Library/Application Support/Cider/config.json`.\n\n10. **Menu bar icon** \u2014 Add an `NSStatusItem` in the menu bar as a secondary access point. Clicking it could toggle sidebar visibility. This also provides a place for settings and quit.\n\n### Design Tokens\n\n```swift\nenum CiderDesign {\n    static let sidebarWidthCollapsed: CGFloat = 72\n    static let sidebarWidthExpanded: CGFloat = 280\n    static let cornerRadius: CGFloat = 16\n    static let componentSpacing: CGFloat = 8\n    static let iconSize: CGFloat = 44\n    static let iconCornerRadius: CGFloat = 12\n    static let animationDuration: Double = 0.3\n    static let hoverExpandWeight: CGFloat = 2.5\n    static let hoverContractWeight: CGFloat = 0.5\n    \n    // Colors (amber/gold cider palette)\n    static let accentColor = Color(hex: \"#f59e0b\")      // Amber\n    static let accentLight = Color(hex: \"#fcd34d\")       // Light gold\n    static let accentDark = Color(hex: \"#d97706\")        // Dark amber\n    static let runningIndicator = Color(hex: \"#22c55e\")  // Green dot for running apps\n    static let textPrimary = Color.white\n    static let textSecondary = Color.white.opacity(0.6)\n    static let textTertiary = Color.white.opacity(0.4)\n    static let separator = Color.white.opacity(0.1)\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## What \"Done\" Looks Like for v0.1\n\nWhen finished, I should be able to:\n\n1. Launch Cider and see a floating glass sidebar on the left edge of my screen\n2. The sidebar shows my pinned apps as squircle icons and a tree list of all open windows grouped by app\n3. I can click a pinned app icon to launch or focus it\n4. I can click any window in the list to bring it to the front\n5. I can hover over the pinned apps section and it smoothly expands while the windows section contracts, and vice versa\n6. Running apps show a green dot indicator\n7. There's a menu bar icon I can click to toggle visibility or quit\n8. The sidebar doesn't steal focus from whatever app I'm working in\n9. The sidebar has the native macOS frosted glass appearance\n10. I can right-click a pinned app to remove it\n\n---\n\n## Important Notes\n\n- This is a real project that will be actively developed. Write clean, well-organized code with proper separation of concerns.\n- Use Swift conventions: protocols for services, structs for models, classes for ViewModels with ObservableObject.\n- Add TODO comments where future features will plug in, referencing the component name (e.g., `// TODO: ClipboardView will go here`).\n- The extension system is important to the long-term architecture. Keep components modular so they could eventually become the \"built-in extensions\" pattern.\n- Don't over-engineer the v0.1 \u2014 keep it simple and working. But don't create technical debt that makes the v0.2\u2013v1.0 features hard to add.\n- Include the Accessibility permission check and user guidance on first launch \u2014 without it, the app is useless.\n- Test on a multi-monitor setup if possible \u2014 even for v0.1, the sidebar should at least work correctly on the primary display.\n",

use numbering config with LevelFormat.BULLET\n   131\tconst doc = new Document({\n   132\t  numbering: {\n   133\t    config: [\n   134\t      { reference: \"bullets\",\n   135\t        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.BULLET, text: \"\u2022\", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,\n   136\t          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },\n   137\t      { reference: \"numbers\",\n   138\t        levels: [{ level: 0, format: LevelFormat.DECIMAL, text: \"%1.\", alignment: AlignmentType.LEFT,\n   139\t          style: { paragraph: { indent: { left: 720, hanging: 360 } } } }] },\n   140\t    ]\n   141\t  },\n   142\t  sections: [{\n   143\t    children: [\n   144\t      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: \"bullets\", level: 0 },\n   145\t        children: [new TextRun(\"Bullet item\")] }),\n   146\t      new Paragraph({ numbering: { reference: \"numbers\", level: 0 },\n   147\t        children: [new TextRun(\"Numbered item\")] }),\n   148\t    ]\n   149\t  }]\n   150\t});\n   151\t\n   152\t// \u26a0\ufe0f Each reference creates INDEPENDENT numbering\n   153\t// Same reference = continues (1,2,3 then 4,5,6)\n   154\t// Different reference = restarts (1,2,3 then 1,2,3)\n   155\t```\n   156\t\n   157\t### Tables\n   158\t\n   159\t**CRITICAL: Tables need dual widths** - set both `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on each cell. Without both, tables render incorrectly on some platforms.\n   160\t\n   161\t```javascript\n   162\t// CRITICAL: Always set table width for consistent rendering\n   163\t// CRITICAL: Use ShadingType.CLEAR (not SOLID) to prevent black backgrounds\n   164\tconst border = { style: BorderStyle.SINGLE, size: 1, color: \"CCCCCC\" };\n   165\tconst borders = { top: border, bottom: border, left: border, right: border };\n   166\t\n   167\tnew Table({\n   168\t  width: { size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }, // Always set table width\n   169\t  columnWidths: [4680, 4680], // Set at table level (DXA: 1440 = 1 inch)\n   170\t  rows: [\n   171\t    new TableRow({\n   172\t      children: [\n   173\t        new TableCell({\n   174\t          borders,\n   175\t          width: { size: 4680, type: WidthType.DXA }, // Also set on each cell\n   176\t          shading: { fill: \"D5E8F0\", type: ShadingType.CLEAR }, // CLEAR not SOLID\n   177\t          margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }, // Cell padding (internal, not added to width)\n   178\t          children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun(\"Cell\")] })]\n   179\t        })\n   180\t      ]\n   181\t    })\n   182\t  ]\n   183\t})\n   184\t```\n   185\t\n   186\t**Table width calculation:**\n   187\t\n   188\tUse `WidthType.PERCENTAGE` for simplicity, or `WidthType.DXA` for precise control:\n   189\t\n   190\t```javascript\n   191\t// Option 1: Percentage (recommended - automatically fits content area)\n   192\twidth: { size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }\n   193\t\n   194\t// Option 2: DXA (precise control)\n   195\t// Table width = sum of columnWidths = content width\n   196\t// US Letter with 1\" margins: 12240 - 2880 = 9360 DXA\n   197\twidth: { size: 9360, type: WidthType.DXA },\n   198\tcolumnWidths: [7000, 2360]  // Must sum to table width\n   199\t```\n   200\t\n   201\t**Width rules:**\n   202\t- Table width must equal the sum of `columnWidths`\n   203\t- Cell `width` must match corresponding `columnWidth`\n   204\t- Cell `margins` are internal padding - they reduce content area, not add to cell width\n   205\t- For full-width tables: use content width (page width minus left and right margins)\n   206\t\n   207\t### Images\n   208\t\n   209\t```javascript\n   210\t// CRITICAL: type parameter is REQUIRED\n   211\tnew Paragraph({\n   212\t  children: [new ImageRun({\n   213\t    type: \"png\", // Required: png, jpg, jpeg, gif, bmp, svg\n   214\t    data: fs.readFileSync(\"image.png\"),\n   215\t    transformation: { width: 200, height: 150 },\n   216\t    altText: { title: \"Title\", description: \"Desc\", name: \"Name\" } // All three required\n   217\t  })]\n   218\t})\n   219\t```\n   220\t\n   221\t### Page Breaks\n   222\t\n   223\t```javascript\n   224\t// CRITICAL: PageBreak must be inside a Paragraph\n   225\tnew Paragraph({ children: [new PageBreak()] })\n   226\t\n   227\t// Or use pageBreakBefore\n   228\tnew Paragraph({ pageBreakBefore: true, children: [new TextRun(\"New page\")] })\n   229\t```\n   230\t\n   231\t### Table of Contents\n   232\t\n   233\t```javascript\n   234\t// CRITICAL: Headings must use HeadingLevel ONLY - no custom styles\n   235\tnew TableOfContents(\"Table of Contents\", { hyperlink: true, headingStyleRange: \"1-3\" })\n   236\t```\n   237\t\n   238\t### Headers/Footers\n   239\t\n   240\t```javascript\n   241\tsections: [{\n   242\t  properties: {\n   243\t    page: { margin: { top: 1440, right: 1440, bottom: 1440, left: 1440 } } // 1440 = 1 inch\n   244\t  },\n   245\t  headers: {\n   246\t    default: new Header({ children: [new Paragraph({ children: [new TextRun(\"Header\")] })] })\n   247\t  },\n   248\t  footers: {\n   249\t    default: new Footer({ children: [new Paragraph({\n   250\t      children: [new TextRun(\"Page \"), new TextRun({ children: [PageNumber.CURRENT] })]\n   251\t    })] })\n   252\t  },\n   253\t  children: [/* content */]\n   254\t}]\n   255\t```\n   256\t\n   257\t### Critical Rules for docx-js\n   258\t\n   259\t- **Set page size explicitly** - docx-js defaults to A4; use US Letter (12240 x 15840 DXA) for US documents\n   260\t- **Never use `\\n`** - use separate Paragraph elements\n   261\t- **Never use unicode bullets** - use `LevelFormat.BULLET` with numbering config\n   262\t- **PageBreak must be in Paragraph** - standalone creates invalid XML\n   263\t- **ImageRun requires `type`** - always specify png/jpg/etc\n   264\t- **Always set table `width`** - use `{ size: 100, type: WidthType.PERCENTAGE }` for full width\n   265\t- **Tables need dual widths** - `columnWidths` array AND cell `width`, both must match\n   266\t- **Table width = sum of columnWidths** - for DXA, ensure they add up exactly\n   267\t- **Always add cell margins** - use `margins: { top: 80, bottom: 80, left: 120, right: 120 }` for readable padding\n   268\t- **Use `ShadingType.CLEAR`** - never SOLID for table shading\n   269\t- **TOC requires HeadingLevel only** - no custom styles on heading paragraphs\n   270\t- **Override built-in styles** - use exact IDs: \"Heading1\", \"Heading2\", etc.\n   271\t- **Include `outlineLevel`** - required for TOC (0 for H1, 1 for H2, etc.)\n   272\t\n   273\t---\n   274\t\n   275\t## Editing Existing Documents\n   276\t\n   277\t**Follow all 3 steps in order.**\n   278\t\n   279\t### Step 1: Unpack\n   280\t```bash\n   281\tpython scripts/office/unpack.py document.docx unpacked/\n   282\t```\n   283\tExtracts XML, pretty-prints, merges adjacent runs, and converts smart quotes to XML entities (`&#x201C;` etc.) so they survive editing. Use `--merge-runs false` to skip run merging.\n   284\t\n   285\t### Step 2: Edit XML\n   286\t\n   287\tEdit files in `unpacked/word/`. See XML Reference below for patterns.\n   288\t\n   289\t**Use \"Claude\" as the author** for tracked changes and comments, unless the user explicitly requests use of a different name.\n   290\t\n   291\t**Use the Edit tool directly for string replacement. Do not write Python scripts.** Scripts introduce unnecessary complexity. The Edit tool shows exactly what is being replaced.\n   292\t\n   293\t**CRITICAL: Use smart quotes for new content.** When adding text with apostrophes or quotes, use XML entities to produce smart quotes:\n   294\t```xml\n   295\t<!-- Use these entities for professional typography -->\n   296\t<w:t>Here&#x2019;s a quote: &#x201C;Hello&#x201D;</w:t>\n   297\t```\n   298\t| Entity | Character |\n   299\t|--------|-----------|\n   300\t| `&#x2018;` | \u2018 (left single) |\n   301\t| `&#x2019;` | \u2019 (right single / apostrophe) |\n   302\t| `&#x201C;` | \u201c (left double) |\n   303\t| `&#x201D;` | \u201d (right double) |\n   304\t\n   305\t**Adding comments:** Use `comment.py` to handle boilerplate across multiple XML files (text must be pre-escaped XML):\n   306\t```bash\n   307\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 \"Comment text with &amp; and &#x2019;\"\n   308\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 1 \"Reply text\" --parent 0  # reply to comment 0\n   309\tpython scripts/comment.py unpacked/ 0 \"Text\" --author \"Custom Author\"  # custom author name\n   310\t```\n   311\tThen add markers to document.xml (see Comments in XML Reference).\n   312\t\n   313\t### Step 3: Pack\n   314\t```bash\n   315\tpython scripts/office/pack.py unpacked/ output.docx --original document.docx\n   316\t```\n   317\tValidates with auto-repair, condenses XML, and creates DOCX. Use `--validate false` to skip.\n   318\t\n   319\t**Auto-repair will fix:**\n   320\t- `durableId` >= 0x7FFFFFFF (regenerates valid ID)\n   321\t- Missing `xml:space=\"preserve\"` on `<w:t>` with whitespace\n   322\t\n   323\t**Auto-repair won't fix:**\n   324\t- Malformed XML, invalid element nesting, missing relationships, schema violations\n   325\t\n   326\t### Common Pitfalls\n   327\t\n   328\t- **Replace entire `<w:r>` elements**: When adding tracked changes, replace the whole `<w:r>...</w:r>` block with `<w:del>...<w:ins>...` as siblings. Don't inject tracked change tags inside a run.\n   329\t- **Preserve `<w:rPr>` formatting**: Copy the original run's `<w:rPr>` block into your tracked change runs to maintain bold, font size, etc.\n   330\t\n   331\t---\n   332\t\n   333\t## XML Reference\n   334\t\n   335\t### Schema Compliance\n   336\t\n   337\t- **Element order in `<w:pPr>`**: `<w:pStyle>`, `<w:numPr>`, `<w:spacing>`, `<w:ind>`, `<w:jc>`, `<w:rPr>` last\n   338\t- **Whitespace**: Add `xml:space=\"preserve\"` to `<w:t>` with leading/trailing spaces\n   339\t- **RSIDs**: Must be 8-digit hex (e.g., `00AB1234`)\n   340\t\n   341\t### Tracked Changes\n   342\t\n   343\t**Insertion:**\n   344\t```xml\n   345\t<w:ins w:id=\"1\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\">\n   346\t  <w:r><w:t>inserted text</w:t></w:r>\n   347\t</w:ins>\n   348\t```\n   349\t\n   350\t**Deletion:**\n   351\t```xml\n   352\t<w:del w:id=\"2\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\">\n   353\t  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>\n   354\t</w:del>\n   355\t```\n   356\t\n   357\t**Inside `<w:del>`**: Use `<w:delText>` instead of `<w:t>`, and `<w:delInstrText>` instead of `<w:instrText>`.\n   358\t\n   359\t**Minimal edits** - only mark what changes:\n   360\t```xml\n   361\t<!-- Change \"30 days\" to \"60 days\" -->\n   362\t<w:r><w:t>The term is </w:t></w:r>\n   363\t<w:del w:id=\"1\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"...\">\n   364\t  <w:r><w:delText>30</w:delText></w:r>\n   365\t</w:del>\n   366\t<w:ins w:id=\"2\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"...\">\n   367\t  <w:r><w:t>60</w:t></w:r>\n   368\t</w:ins>\n   369\t<w:r><w:t> days.</w:t></w:r>\n   370\t```\n   371\t\n   372\t**Deleting entire paragraphs/list items** - when removing ALL content from a paragraph, also mark the paragraph mark as deleted so it merges with the next paragraph. Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:\n   373\t```xml\n   374\t<w:p>\n   375\t  <w:pPr>\n   376\t    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->\n   377\t    <w:rPr>\n   378\t      <w:del w:id=\"1\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\"/>\n   379\t    </w:rPr>\n   380\t  </w:pPr>\n   381\t  <w:del w:id=\"2\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\">\n   382\t    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>\n   383\t  </w:del>\n   384\t</w:p>\n   385\t```\n   386\tWithout the `<w:del/>` in `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph/list item.\n   387\t\n   388\t**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:\n   389\t```xml\n   390\t<w:ins w:author=\"Jane\" w:id=\"5\">\n   391\t  <w:del w:author=\"Claude\" w:id=\"10\">\n   392\t    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>\n   393\t  </w:del>\n   394\t</w:ins>\n   395\t```\n   396\t\n   397\t**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):\n   398\t```xml\n   399\t<w:del w:author=\"Jane\" w:id=\"5\">\n   400\t  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>\n   401\t</w:del>\n   402\t<w:ins w:author=\"Claude\" w:id=\"10\">\n   403\t  <w:r><w:t>deleted text</w:t></w:r>\n   404\t</w:ins>\n   405\t```\n   406\t\n   407\t### Comments\n   408\t\n   409\tAfter running `comment.py` (see Step 2), add markers to document.xml. For replies, use `--parent` flag and nest markers inside the parent's.\n   410\t\n   411\t**CRITICAL: `<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` are siblings of `<w:r>`, never inside `<w:r>`.**\n   412\t\n   413\t```xml\n   414\t<!-- Comment markers are direct children of w:p, never inside w:r -->\n   415\t<w:commentRangeStart w:id=\"0\"/>\n   416\t<w:del w:id=\"1\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\">\n   417\t  <w:r><w:delText>deleted</w:delText></w:r>\n   418\t</w:del>\n   419\t<w:r><w:t> more text</w:t></w:r>\n   420\t<w:commentRangeEnd w:id=\"0\"/>\n   421\t<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val=\"CommentReference\"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id=\"0\"/></w:r>\n   422\t\n   423\t<!-- Comment 0 with reply 1 nested inside -->\n   424\t<w:commentRangeStart w:id=\"0\"/>\n   425\t  <w:commentRangeStart w:id=\"1\"/>\n   426\t  <w:r><w:t>text</w:t></w:r>\n   427\t  <w:commentRangeEnd w:id=\"1\"/>\n   428\t<w:commentRangeEnd w:id=\"0\"/>\n   429\t<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val=\"CommentReference\"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id=\"0\"/></w:r>\n   430\t<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val=\"CommentReference\"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id=\"1\"/></w:r>\n   431\t```\n   432\t\n   433\t### Images\n   434\t\n   435\t1. Add image file to `word/media/`\n   436\t2. Add relationship to `word/_rels/document.xml.rels`:\n   437\t```xml\n   438\t<Relationship Id=\"rId5\" Type=\".../image\" Target=\"media/image1.png\"/>\n   439\t```\n   440\t3. Add content type to `[Content_Types].xml`:\n   441\t```xml\n   442\t<Default Extension=\"png\" ContentType=\"image/png\"/>\n   443\t```\n   444\t4. Reference in document.xml:\n   445\t```xml\n   446\t<w:drawing>\n   447\t  <wp:inline>\n   448\t    <wp:extent cx=\"914400\" cy=\"914400\"/>  <!-- EMUs: 914400 = 1 inch -->\n   449\t    <a:graphic>\n   450\t      <a:graphicData uri=\".../picture\">\n   451\t        <pic:pic>\n   452\t          <pic:blipFill><a:blip r:embed=\"rId5\"/></pic:blipFill>\n   453\t        </pic:pic>\n   454\t      </a:graphicData>\n   455\t    </a:graphic>\n   456\t  </wp:inline>\n   457\t</w:drawing>\n   458\t```\n   459\t\n   460\t---\n   461\t\n   462\t## Dependencies\n   463\t\n   464\t- **pandoc**: Text extraction\n   465\t- **docx**: `npm install -g docx` (new documents)\n   466\t- **LibreOffice**: PDF conversion (auto-configured for sandboxed environments via `scripts/office/soffice.py`)\n   467\t- **Poppler**: `pdftoppm` for images\n   468\t",

\"Arial\", size: 22, color: GRAY_MED })\n    ]\n  });\n}\nfunction numbered(text, ref = \"numbers\") {\n  return new Paragraph({\n    numbering: { reference: ref, level: 0 },\n    spacing: { after: 60 Add `<w:del/>` inside `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`:\n   373\t```xml\n   374\t<w:p>\n   375\t  <w:pPr>\n   376\t    <w:numPr>...</w:numPr>  <!-- list numbering if present -->\n   377\t    <w:rPr>\n   378\t      <w:del w:id=\"1\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\"/>\n   379\t    </w:rPr>\n   380\t  </w:pPr>\n   381\t  <w:del w:id=\"2\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\">\n   382\t    <w:r><w:delText>Entire paragraph content being deleted...</w:delText></w:r>\n   383\t  </w:del>\n   384\t</w:p>\n   385\t```\n   386\tWithout the `<w:del/>` in `<w:pPr><w:rPr>`, accepting changes leaves an empty paragraph/list item.\n   387\t\n   388\t**Rejecting another author's insertion** - nest deletion inside their insertion:\n   389\t```xml\n   390\t<w:ins w:author=\"Jane\" w:id=\"5\">\n   391\t  <w:del w:author=\"Claude\" w:id=\"10\">\n   392\t    <w:r><w:delText>their inserted text</w:delText></w:r>\n   393\t  </w:del>\n   394\t</w:ins>\n   395\t```\n   396\t\n   397\t**Restoring another author's deletion** - add insertion after (don't modify their deletion):\n   398\t```xml\n   399\t<w:del w:author=\"Jane\" w:id=\"5\">\n   400\t  <w:r><w:delText>deleted text</w:delText></w:r>\n   401\t</w:del>\n   402\t<w:ins w:author=\"Claude\" w:id=\"10\">\n   403\t  <w:r><w:t>deleted text</w:t></w:r>\n   404\t</w:ins>\n   405\t```\n   406\t\n   407\t### Comments\n   408\t\n   409\tAfter running `comment.py` (see Step 2), add markers to document.xml. For replies, use `--parent` flag and nest markers inside the parent's.\n   410\t\n   411\t**CRITICAL: `<w:commentRangeStart>` and `<w:commentRangeEnd>` are siblings of `<w:r>`, never inside `<w:r>`.**\n   412\t\n   413\t```xml\n   414\t<!-- Comment markers are direct children of w:p, never inside w:r -->\n   415\t<w:commentRangeStart w:id=\"0\"/>\n   416\t<w:del w:id=\"1\" w:author=\"Claude\" w:date=\"2025-01-01T00:00:00Z\">\n   417\t  <w:r><w:delText>deleted</w:delText></w:r>\n   418\t</w:del>\n   419\t<w:r><w:t> more text</w:t></w:r>\n   420\t<w:commentRangeEnd w:id=\"0\"/>\n   421\t<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val=\"CommentReference\"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id=\"0\"/></w:r>\n   422\t\n   423\t<!-- Comment 0 with reply 1 nested inside -->\n   424\t<w:commentRangeStart w:id=\"0\"/>\n   425\t  <w:commentRangeStart w:id=\"1\"/>\n   426\t  <w:r><w:t>text</w:t></w:r>\n   427\t  <w:commentRangeEnd w:id=\"1\"/>\n   428\t<w:commentRangeEnd w:id=\"0\"/>\n   429\t<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val=\"CommentReference\"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id=\"0\"/></w:r>\n   430\t<w:r><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val=\"CommentReference\"/></w:rPr><w:commentReference w:id=\"1\"/></w:r>\n   431\t```\n   432\t\n   433\t### Images\n   434\t\n   435\t1. Each extension runs in its own sandboxed XPC service process, communicates with Cider through a defined protocol, and can't crash the main app. This is how Apple's own extension points work (Finder Sync extensions, Share extensions, etc.) and it's the pattern users and developers on macOS expect.\n\nBut you don't build XPC plumbing now. Name them semantically so agents use `Spacing.sectionGap` instead of guessing a number.\n\n**Corner radii:**\n\nSame problem. Without a defined scale, you get 6px here, 8px there, 12px somewhere else. macOS generally uses: 4-6 for small elements (buttons, tags), 8-10 for cards and list items, 12-16 for panels and popovers, and the continuous corner radius (squircle) for app icons. Define these once, name them, done.\n\n**Shadows and elevation:**\n\nFloating panels need shadows to feel like they're hovering above the desktop. But the shadow parameters need to be consistent \u2014 a companion window should have the same shadow as the sidebar, and both should match what macOS does natively. Define two or three elevation levels: subtle (for hover states and slight lifts), medium (for the sidebar and companion windows), and strong (for drag-in-progress states). Each level specifies radius, offset, opacity, and color.\n\n**Typography:**\n\nSince you're using SF Pro (the system font), you mostly just need to define which dynamic type styles map to which UI elements. Sidebar section headers might use `.headline`, window list items might use `.body`, metadata and timestamps might use `.caption`. The key is that every agent uses the same style for the same kind of content.\n\n**Animation tokens:**\n\nThis is what the debug panel will help you define. Once you've tuned each animation, it gets a name and exact parameters. Every future agent session references these tokens instead of inventing new animations. Categories would be: transitions (panel appear/disappear, section expand/collapse), interactions (hover, press, drag), and feedback (save indicator, notification pulse, error shake).\n\n**Component patterns:**\n\nBeyond raw tokens, you want to define how recurring UI patterns are built. How does a list item look and behave \u2014 what's the height, the padding, the hover state, the selected state, the right-click behavior? How does a section header look \u2014 what font, what color, does it have a disclosure triangle, how does it animate open/closed? How does a button look \u2014 size variants, states (normal, hover, pressed, disabled), the animation between states?\n\nThis matters more than it seems because Cider will have a lot of repeated patterns: the pinned apps list, the window list, the clipboard history list, the bookmarks grid, the notes list in the library. If each one is built slightly differently because a different agent session made different assumptions, the app feels inconsistent. If they all reference the same `CiderListItem` component pattern, everything matches.\n\n**Iconography:**\n\nSF Symbols is the obvious choice \u2014 Apple's icon library that matches the system perfectly. Define which symbol weight you use (regular, medium, or semibold), which rendering mode (monochrome, hierarchical, or palette), and which size category. Consistency here means every icon in the sidebar has the same visual weight.\n\n**Toasts and notifications:**\n\nWhen Cider needs to tell the user something (note saved, bookmark captured, OCR complete, error occurred), how does that look? A small toast that slides in from the top of the sidebar? A subtle highlight on the relevant section? A system notification? Define the pattern once: position, size, animation in/out, duration before auto-dismiss, color coding for different message types (success, info, warning, error).\n\n**What I'd suggest building:**\n\nI can create a comprehensive design system document that covers all of this \u2014 color tokens, spacing scale, typography scale, animation tokens (with placeholder values you'll tune with the debug panel), component patterns, and interaction specifications. It would be a markdown file that lives in your repo alongside the VISION.md and ARCHITECTURE.md, and it becomes the first thing any agent reads before touching UI code.\n\nWant me to put that together? I'd structure it as a practical reference \u2014 not a theoretical design doc, but something an LLM agent can directly translate into Swift constants and SwiftUI modifiers.",

It was announced on June 9, 2025, at the Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC). Liquid Glass features a fluid, dynamic glass-like interface that reflects and refracts the background. Liquid Glass was introduced in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, and watchOS 26. Apple sought a new design language to unify the look and feel of interface elements across its devices, with their various window sizes and displays. It describes Liquid Glass as a dynamic \"material\" that combines the \"optical properties of glass with a sense of fluidity\". According to Apple's updated human interface guidelines, apps made with Liquid Glass should showcase hierarchy between content and controls. The design features elements that automatically adapt to their environment by reflecting and refracting light.\n\nApp icons have been redesigned to use a layered system akin to the one used on visionOS and tvOS, applying translucency and a glass-like shimmer effect, which also reacts to device movement, while applying greater use of gradients. Toolbars and other elements on-screen are now no-longer pinned to the device's bezels, instead being separated into bubbles that appear and disappear based on the context. For example, the Music app's tab bar shrinks when scrolling. The new design also allows the material to change its shape and size, such as the text selection tooltip expanding to show all options in a vertical list. In a video detailing the design change, Apple stated that the language was influenced by the Aqua design language of macOS, real-time Gaussian blurring in iOS 7, the motion in iPhone X, the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 14 Pro an\n\nThe design marked a shift in Apple's design languages, moving away from some of the flat design cues popularized by Jony Ive in iOS 7 (2013) toward more expressive, skeuomorphic elements. Many critics and social media users noted similarities to Aqua and Windows Aero, including glass-like textures popularized by Windows Vista. Liquid Glass has strong influences from \"glassmorphism\", a design style that became popular in 2021 in part by Microsoft's Windows 11 and its use of Fluent Design as well as Apple's own macOS Big Sur. Liquid Glass has had a mixed reception. Some reviewers praised the way it recreates glass's refracting and lensing properties. Others have criticized it as distracting, less legible, harder to use, and an undue burden on developers.         "text": "To support devices running iOS versions earlier than 26, developers can create a custom view modifier that conditionally applies the glassEffect or a fallback implementation. The fallback can use existing SwiftUI materials, such as .ultraThinMaterial, combined with gradients and strokes to ...\n\nApple\u2019s iOS 26 introduces a new visual style with the glassEffect modifier in SwiftUI, enabling developers to apply a translucent, glass-like appearance to views. This article explains how to use the glassEffect modifier, clarifies the role of the interactive parameter, and provides a method to maintain compatibility with earlier iOS versions. The glassEffect modifier, available in iOS 26 and later, applies a glass-like material to a SwiftUI view. It requires a shape parameter to define the area where the effect is applied and an optional style parameter to specify the material\u2019s appearance. The modifier can also enable interactivity, allowing the effect to respond to user interactions. Here\u2019s an example of how to implement the glassEffect modifier: import SwiftUI struct ContentView: View { var body: some View { VStack { Text(\"Sample Text\") .padding() .glassEffect(.regular.interactive(), in: .circle) Spacer() } .padding() } } In this code, the glassEffect is applied to a Text view with\n\nFor iOS 26 and later, it applies the native glassEffect modifier, with an option for interactivity.         "text": "According to Apple&#x27;s updated human interface guidelines, apps made with Liquid Glass should showcase hierarchy between content and controls. The design features elements that automatically ...\n\nLiquid Glass is a design language developed by Apple as a unified visual theme for the graphical user interfaces for its suite of operating systems. It was announced on June 9, 2025, at the Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC). Liquid Glass features a fluid, dynamic glass-like interface that reflects and refracts the background. Liquid Glass was introduced in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, tvOS 26, visionOS 26, and watchOS 26. Apple sought a new design language to unify the look and feel of interface elements across its devices, with their various window sizes and displays. It describes Liquid Glass as a dynamic \"material\" that combines the \"optical properties of glass with a sense of fluidity\". According to Apple's updated human interface guidelines, apps made with Liquid Glass should showcase hierarchy between content and controls. The design features elements that automatically adapt to their environment by reflecting and refracting light.\n\nApp icons have been redesigned to use a layered system akin to the one used on visionOS and tvOS, applying translucency and a glass-like shimmer effect, which also reacts to device movement, while applying greater use of gradients. App icons can now adopt a new clear look that makes the background use the Liquid Glass material in a light or dark tint, making it appear transparent. Toolbars and other elements on-screen are now no-longer pinned to the device's bezels, instead being separated into bubbles that appear and disappear based on the context. For example, the Music app's tab bar shrinks when scrolling. The new design also allows the material to change its shape and size, such as the text selection tooltip expanding to show all options in a vertical list. In a video detailing the design change, Apple stated that the language was influenced by the Aqua design language of macOS, real-time Gaussian blurring in iOS 7, the motion in iPhone X, the Dynamic Island on the iPhone 14 Pro an\n\nThe design marked a shift in Apple's design languages, moving away from some of the flat design cues popularized by Jony Ive in iOS 7 (2013) toward more expressive, skeuomorphic elements. Many critics and social media users noted similarities to Aqua and Windows Aero, including glass-like textures popularized by Windows Vista. Liquid Glass has strong influences from \"glassmorphism\", a design style that became popular in 2021 in part by Microsoft's Windows 11 and its use of Fluent Design as well as Apple's own macOS Big Sur. Liquid Glass has had a mixed reception. Some reviewers praised the way it recreates glass's refracting and lensing properties. Others have criticized it as distracting, less legible, harder to use, and an undue burden on developers. Designers interviewed by Wired felt that the visual effects distracted from app content, and one said developers with smaller teams might struggle to meet the complicated visual standards set by the new interface.",

There are four Inspector categories, each of which displays parameter controls for the selected object: Properties Inspector: Contains controls for setting basic attributes of the selected object, such as position, scale, and blending. Behaviors Inspector: Contains controls for adjusting attributes of behaviors\u2014animation and simulation effects that you can apply to objects in your project. Filters Inspector: Contains controls for adjusting attributes of filters\u2014visual treatments that you can apply to objects in your project. Object Inspector: Contains controls that vary depending on the type of object selected. The name of this Inspector is also context-sensitive, changing depending on the type of object selected, such as Camera, Text, or Shape.\n\nKeyframe Editor: Displays the animation curves for animated parameters and effects.",
